messages:
Maria P.: FYI customer POC is blocked, getting 401s and 'scope_mismatch' errors when calling /v1/generate. They say their key used to work.
Alex S.: which key are they using? org or project-scoped? any chance they copied the playground key?
Maria P.: they pasted the service key from their portal. error from client: \"error: invalid_key OR scope_mismatch\". No other details.
Samir R.: ask them to send the curl they run and the `Authorization` header (redact key). often it's `Authorization: Bearer <token>` vs old `X-Api-Key`.
Maria P.: pasted their command: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-ABC123" -d '{"model":"redwood-large","input":"hi"}'`
Jenny (support): ok can they paste the full response headers? we need `x-rw-org` / `x-rw-project` headers sometimes in on-prem setups, but hosted should infer from key binding.
Samir R.: also check the key binding: many customers accidentally create a key scoped to a different project/org. If they created the key under their sandbox org but are calling a POC project id, that'll be scope_mismatch.
Maria P.: customer says they have `org: acme-corp` and project `poc-2026`. How can they verify binding?
Alex S.: tell them to run `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/keys/inspect` (we have an inspect endpoint). response shows `owner_org` and `scopes`.
Maria P.: they ran inspect, returned `owner_org: acme-team`, `scopes: ["embeddings:read"]`. so the key only has embeddings.
Samir R.: that's the culprit. They need `inference:invoke` (and optionally `chat:stream` or `models:use`). Quick fix: create a new key with the right scopes or update key binding in console.
Liz (security): remind them to follow the security questionnaire guidance: don't create broad `*` scopes unless necessary. For POCs we recommend creating a short-lived key with exactly `inference:invoke` and set an expiry.
Maria P.: can we suggest a minimal command they can run to repro once they rotate key?
Samir R.: yes: ```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-poc-REPLACE" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-small","input":"hello"}'
```
Samir R.: if they still get 401, capture full response headers and the `x-rw-rate-limit` headers; also share `request-id` from the body so we can trace on infra side.
Jenny (support): I can open a trace if they give us `request-id`. infra-bot, can you thumbs-up to indicate readiness to trace?
infra-bot: :white_check_mark: infra tracing ready — include `request-id` and I'll pull the logs.
Maria P.: customer rotating key now and will test. Also asked about pricing impact for POC if we ask them to create a new scoped key — they are worried about accidental charges.
Alex S.: reassure: creating a scoped key doesn't change billing; usage accrues to the account/project that invoked the request. We can also set a spend limit on the project for POC.
Liz (security): add note: rotate frequently and restrict IPs if needed (console supports IP allowlist for keys).
Maria P.: they tested new key with `inference:invoke` scope — success! got 200 and tokens back. ✅
Alex S.: great — can we close the POC blocker? any follow-ups?
Maria P.: I'll send the customer a checklist: inspect key binding, minimal scopes, rotate keys, set spend limit, capture `request-id` for debugging. Thanks everyone! :tada:
